final.executive_summary: Underweight AAPL and rebalance to 6% of total account equity (~$5,992 / ~19.4 shares at the 309.38 mark), selling ~13.55 shares (~$4,192 proceeds, ~$4.19 fee at 10 bps), executed at the unknown next open. This 6% is an independent total-target reassessment, not another mechanical proportional discount off yesterday's 10.2%: it sits between a concrete higher 0.10-0.15 (which would require believing the below-consensus guide and supply constraints are already fully discounted and that the 300-302 shelf holds) and a concrete lower 0.00-0.03 (justified only on a decisive break of 300, gross margin below 48%, or no Q4 reacceleration). I knowingly accept the cash opportunity cost of ~94% idle, non-interest-bearing cash - forgoing a reclaim of 320.45-323.84 and a gap-fill toward 333-340 - because another 10% decline costs ~0.6% of total equity at 6% versus ~1.0% at 10.2% and ~1.5% at 15%. The residual 6% is not an 'observation stub': at ~$5,992 it is a real participation stake (~0.6% of total equity per 10% move) that keeps the genuine reported cash-flow strength and rebound optionality in the account, which is preferable to zero only because the 200SMA trend, $62.17B net cash and 30% FCF margin remain intact and fees would otherwise be paid twice to exit and re-enter.
final.investment_thesis: The direction is genuinely contested and the bear wins on the forward-looking evidence that governs sizing, while the bull wins enough on the rear-view fundamentals to foreclose zero exposure. Bull side, unrebutted: the fresh 10-Q shows nine-month revenue +16.2%, EPS +22.4%, FCF +52.5%, gross margin 50.06%, net cash $62.17B, and price at 309.38 sits +11.07% above a still-rising 200SMA at 278.54; volume faded into the 300 retest (132.49M -> 68.00M) and the June shock was fully retraced in five sessions. That is why this is Underweight and not Sell, and why the target is 6% rather than 0-3%. Bear side, decisive for the size: the stock de-rated not on a weak reported quarter but on guidance below consensus plus management-flagged supply constraints; margin expansion is entirely gross-margin dependent (opex +21.9% versus revenue +16.2%, no operating leverage) with gross margin at 50.06% described as a cyclical high, so each 100 bp of give-back is roughly $4.9B pre-tax / $0.28 EPS and a move below the 48% tripwire materially damages the EPS story; the 12% buyback cut removes per-share support; deferred revenue +8.8% versus revenue +16.2% is a soft Services-bookings signal on the exact mix engine underpinning the margin thesis; the +260% raw-materials build creates inventory write-down risk if Q4 does not reaccelerate; and the ~$13B gross-intangible increase is not underwritten as bullish optionality without notes. Technically the near-term read is bearish: 309.38 is below the 10EMA at 320.45 and VWMA at 323.70, the entire July volume cohort is overhead supply, MACD is in a bearish cross (histogram -3.521) with RSI 44.68, and the 07-31 gap -8.6% on 132.49M shares (~2.4x average) with ATR repriced +21.3% to 9.775 proves stops below the 300.00 shelf can be gapped through. Weighing prior lessons: my repeated AAPL Underweights (2026-06-30, 2026-07-01, 2026-07-13, 2026-07-22, 2026-07-23) bled alpha because they trimmed on proximity to resistance or a single momentum divergence inside a fully stacked rising structure, without a printed trigger. This setup is different in kind: the 07-31 earnings-driven gap with 2.4x volume is the actual distribution event those reflections demanded as a prerequisite, and the 2026-07-28 reflection's rule - when the stated risk is a dated binary event, size the pre-event trim at the heavier end rather than waiting for a close-basis confirmation a gap will skip - is precisely why I do not wait for a 320.45 reclaim before reducing now. The opposite prior lesson (AMZN/GOOGL: don't express tactical caution as a directional bearish short into an unresolved catalyst) is respected because 6% keeps meaningful upside participation and the position is post-event, not pre-event. Conflicting arguments alone are not a reason to Hold: three of three risk seats converged on 6%, and the dispute was framing (conservative calling 6% a risk ceiling, neutral calling it symmetric), not magnitude, so I commit to Underweight at 6%. What would change it: a decisive close above 320.45-323.84 on improving volume lifts the target toward 0.08-0.10; a decisive close below 300, gross margin trending below 48%, or a Q4 print with no revenue reacceleration cuts toward 0.03 or zero. Explicit data gaps: no exact guidance/EPS consensus figures, no valuation multiples (P/E, EV/FCF, FCF yield), and no insider-transaction data are supplied, so 'already down 9%' is not proof of cheapness and no valuation-based price target is issued.
